taxonomyNote: NatureServe's standard common name is 'Little Brown Skink'; 'Ground Skink' is listed as an alternate name.
fieldMarks: Tiny skink with smooth, shiny scales, cylindrical body, conical head and short legs; light tan to golden-brown above.
Dark brown to black stripe along each side extending onto the tail; belly white or yellow.
Total length averages about 146 mm (75-146 mm range); females have larger heads, males longer tails.
Juveniles are bronze with black specks; adults can drop and regrow the tail.
behavior: Diurnal and ground-dwelling, basking and moving through leaf litter; generally does not climb.
Active March-October in the north and all year in Florida; goes underground in cold weather.
Eats termites, millipedes, roaches, ants, beetle larvae, caterpillars and other small arthropods, finding prey by sight and smell.
habitat: Humid deciduous forest, dry upland woodland, stream and pond edges, and vacant lots or building edges in suburbs, always where ground cover (leaf litter, logs, rocks) is present.
range: Eastern and central-eastern United States (NatureServe: Alabama, Arkansas, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Jersey, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia) and northern Mexico; not in Canada.
